source.title: Rethinking Language Model Scaling under Transferable Hypersphere Optimization
source.authors: Liliang Ren; Yang Liu; Ye-Long Shen; Wei-Zhu Chen

record.tranche_reason: It measures validation loss across training compute and fits loss–FLOPs trajectories to power-law curves, testing the compute-scaling part of V1 under a different optimizer and training setup.
record.gate_note: The paper fits loss versus FLOPs, but does not report the fitted exponents. Its token-budget sweep reports fitted optimal learning rates and minimum losses, not a fitted power law for loss versus tokens. Learning-rate transfer results, compute-efficiency leverage, stability metrics, and cited scaling-law results are not rows for the claim versions unless they measure the version’s specified loss behavior. It does not test loss prediction from small runs or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.test_reason: The study fits final validation loss against training FLOPs, L = A·C^-b + C0, for dense and MoE language models from 2.1e19 to 6e21 FLOPs. It does this under different optimizers and learning-rate transfer schemes, so it bears on whether loss falls as a power law in compute (V1). It also shows that the fitted curve and floor depend on the optimizer and parameterization (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but vague. The authors conclude that scaling laws depend critically on the optimizer and parameterization. Under HyperP, a single small-scale learning rate transfers across scales, giving the lowest dense loss floor and 1.58x CEL over Muon at 6e21 FLOPs, with the gain growing with scale. MoE adds 3.38x CEL. The 0.32 exponent concerns the optimal learning rate, not loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Frobenius-sphere MuonH/HyperP optimization and Transformer-Next models, with token-to-parameter scaling set to 50 TPP; it is not a reproduction of the original scaling-law studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with optimizer and learning-rate transfer scheme, depth scaling, and architecture. The optimal learning-rate estimates also vary with the number of LR sweep points; the paper reports different LR optima with and without Depth-µP.

fits_no_version.finding: At 208M active parameters, the optimal loss falls as a power law in MoE sparsity S from 1 to 32. The loss drops 0.224 overall (Table 10, Figure 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss follows a power law in MoE sparsity at fixed active parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal learning rate follows a power law in training tokens, η* ∝ T^-0.32, and in batch size, ∝ B^0.558.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal hyperparameters scale as power laws in tokens and batch size.

record.problems: The loss–FLOPs fit exponents are not reported. Compute-scaling evidence is limited to the tested Transformer-Next configurations and the stated compute range. The token sweep provides fitted minimum losses but does not fit a loss-versus-token power law. The authors note that their Chinchilla assumption may need refitting for each dataset and that extension to other architectures and larger scales remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported validation-loss results for the tested compute trajectories were left out. Results on fitted optimal learning rates, stability indicators, auxiliary load balancing, and architecture stability effects were not included because they do not measure the loss-scaling behavior named by the tested version.

untested.parts: Loss versus parameters alone, or tokens alone, with the other not a bottleneck. Parameters and tokens are co-scaled at 50 TPP, and the token sweep (r24–r28) is not fitted. The fitted exponent b is not reported.
Dependence on parameter counting, data or fitting method. Whether the compute-optimal split changes: the authors assume Chinchilla 50 TPP.
Not tested. The parameter/token split is fixed, not optimised.
Not tested. Shape is held at aspect ratio 128.
Not tested. Text pretraining only; the MoE results are still text.

missing.what: Fitted irreducible floors C0 per method (0.85 HyperP, 1.23 Muon, 1.62 MuonH, 0.87 MoE), which bear on V7
Compute efficiency leverage by depth: HyperP 0.99x to 1.58x; MuonH 0.96x, 1.19x, 1.17x, 0.99x, 0.70x
Loss versus parameters at a fixed 10.4B tokens, d=8–24, with and without Depth-µP (2.47 down to 2.13)

record.verdict_notes: No fitted exponents b are reported, so the compute power law cannot be compared numerically with Kaplan or Chinchilla. The token sweep (r24–r28) shows loss falling monotonically over a 16x token range at 208M parameters, but it is unfitted. The authors assume Chinchilla TPP without refitting it.

versions.untested_parts: Tests validation loss versus training FLOPs for its model and optimizer configurations. It does not establish the loss law separately versus parameter count or training tokens.
The paper transfers learning rates from smaller settings, but does not test whether loss power laws fitted on small runs predict loss for runs orders of magnitude larger.
It scales tokens proportionally to parameter count using 50 TPP for FLOPs scaling; it does not optimize the parameter/token split at fixed compute or fit their growth exponents.
Architecture variants are compared, but not at a fixed parameter count to test the effects of depth, width, or other architecture details.
The study concerns language-model pretraining and does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance is measured.

The study examines sensitivity of fitted optimal learning rates to sweep-point selection, but does not test whether loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation depend on setup or fitting choices, nor whether loss curves bend away from a single power law.
